visual: Tall architectural stems · dense spherical lilac-pink flowerheads · broad grey-green basal leaves
water: Water during active growth if conditions are dry; reduce watering once dormant
soil: Fertile, well-drained; acid, neutral or alkaline
soilWarning: Requires free drainage; avoid wet or waterlogged soil, particularly during winter
prune: No pruning required; remove spent flower stems if desired and clear foliage once it has yellowed naturally
toxicity: Allium species can be harmful if eaten, particularly to pets; ornamental bulbs are not for consumption
resilience: Very hardy and generally pest-free; may be affected by onion white rot and downy mildew
uses: Architectural borders · gravel gardens · wildlife gardens · cut flowers · dried seedheads
container: Suitable for large, deep containers with excellent drainage
